'''Albert Galiyevich Nasibulin''' ({{langx|ru|Альбе́рт Гали́йевич Насибу́лин}}, born 23 March 1972 in [[Novokuznetsk]] city, [[Kemerovo Region]], USSR) is a Russian material scientist recognized for the contributions to synthesis of nanoparticles and carbon nanotubes. He is a professor at [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology]] (Moscow, Russia).

== Career ==
Nasibulin graduated from the Chemical Department of [[Kemerovo State University]] (KemSU, Russia) in 1994. He earned the degrees of Candidate of chemical sciences (1996, KemSU) and [[Doktor nauk]] in technical sciences (2011, [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|St.-Petersburg State Technical University]], Russia).<ref name="R1">[https://faculty.skoltech.ru/people/albertnasibulin Personal profile] of Prof. Nasibulin on the [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology|SkolTech]] site.</ref>

From 1999 to 2014, he worked in Finland: until 2002 he was a senior researcher at the [[VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland]] ({{langx|fi|Teknologian tutkimuskeskus VTT Oy}}), and since 2003 a senior scientist, docent and adjunct professor at the Department of Applied Physics of [[Helsinki University of Technology]] (current name: [[Aalto University]], {{langx|fi|Aalto-yliopiston teknillinen korkeakoulu}}). In 2006-2011, he received an Academy Fellow position from the [[Academy of Finland]].<ref name="R1"/><ref name="R2">[https://research.aalto.fi/en/persons/albert-nasibulin(a9da20db-a604-415b-b26d-867e20b0c5d4).html Personal profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408180012/https://research.aalto.fi/en/persons/albert-nasibulin(a9da20db-a604-415b-b26d-867e20b0c5d4).html |date=2019-04-08 }} of Prof. Nasibulin on [[Aalto University]] site.</ref>

In 2014, Nasibulin returned to Russia and joined the [[Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology]] (Skoltech). Now he is a professor at the Center for Photonic Science and Engineering of the Skoltech and a head of the Laboratory of Nanomaterials. Until 2022, he held an adjunct professorship at Aalto University.

== Research activities ==
Nasibulin specialises on synthesis of [[nanomaterials]] (carbon nanotubes, nanoparticles and nanowires), investigation of their growth mechanisms and applications. He is known for the original aerosol [[Chemical vapor deposition|CVD]] methods of the synthesis of multi-walled and single-walled [[Carbon nanotube|CNTs]]. Nasibulin developed a dry transfer technique to prepare conductive, flexible and transparent coating for [[Indium tin oxide|ITO]] replacement and freestanding single-walled CNT films to fabricate the state-of-the-art key components for several high-impact application areas. He proposed a method for rapid and controlled synthesis of metal oxide nanowires.

Nasibulin is a co-founder of three companies: [https://canatu.com/ Canatu Ltd.] (spin-off from Helsinki University of Technology) and CryptoChemistry and Novaprint (spin-offs from Skoltech). He chaired several conferences<ref name="R4">Information about the role of Prof. Nasibulin as organizer of scientific fora: [http://empnm2018.skoltech.ru/ EMPNM-III] (2018), [https://empnm.skoltech.ru/ EMPNM-VIII] (2024), [http://nt13.aalto.fi/organization.html NT13] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181203210817/http://nt13.aalto.fi/organization.html |date=2018-12-03 }} (2013), [http://nt13.aalto.fi/satellites/NCC13/contact.html NCC] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210107190810/http://nt13.aalto.fi/satellites/NCC13/contact.html |date=2021-01-07 }} (2013), [http://tfy.tkk.fi/nanomat/NDTCS_files/Page2394.htm NDTCS-2011] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430140244/http://tfy.tkk.fi/nanomat/NDTCS_files/Page2394.htm |date=2019-04-30 }} (2011),
[http://bic-fm.skoltech.ru BIC-FM] (2020).</ref> and served as expert or reviewer for various journals<ref name="R5">[https://www.mdpi.com/journal/nanomaterials/editors Editorial Board] of the Nanomaterials open access journal, [https://academic.oup.com/ooenergy/pages/editorial-board Editorial Board] of the Oxford Open Energy journal.</ref> and national/international scientific programs.

== Awards ==
* 2010:  ''FAAR (Finnish Association for Aerosol Research) award'' for Excellent work in Aerosol Science at International Aerosol Conference in Helsinki, Finland.<ref name="R6">List of [http://www.atm.helsinki.fi/FAAR/index.php?page=news FAAR award recipients] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425163121/http://www.atm.helsinki.fi/FAAR/index.php?page=news |date=2019-04-25 }}.</ref>
* 2011: ''Smoluchowski award'' for the contribution to field of "Aerosol synthesis and mechanistic investigations of carbon nanotubes" at European Aerosol Conference in Manchester, UK.<ref name="R7">Information about the Smoluchowski Award and the [http://www.info.gaef.de/kopie-von-smoluchowski-award List of its winners] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408180004/http://www.info.gaef.de/kopie-von-smoluchowski-award |date=2019-04-08 }}.</ref>
* 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024: The Best Professor of SkolTech in various nominations.<ref name="R8">[https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2017/06/life-lessons-from-some-of-skoltech-s-leading-professors/ Life lessons from some of Skoltech’s leading professors] (2017),  
[https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2019/07/skoltech-commencement-ceremony-2019/ Skoltech commencement ceremony] (2019), [https://www.skoltech.ru/en/2022/07/skoltech-commencement-ceremony-2022-2/ Skoltech commencement ceremony] (2022), [https://new.skoltech.ru/en/news/yubilejnyj-vypusknoj-skolteha-kak-proshla-osobennaya-ceremoniya Skoltech Jubilee Commencement Ceremony] (2024) — ceremonies of honoring the best professors, incl. Nasibulin.</ref>  
* 2018: Honorary title of the [[Professor of the Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="R9">[http://www.ras.ru/presidium/documents/directions.aspx?ID=c67b9e8d-731c-4456-b26b-1fb3b7135046 Decree of the Presidium of the Russian Academy of Sciences No. 65 dated 04.24.2018] on awarding the title “Professor of the RAS” (in Russian).</ref>
* 2019: Gold medal named after academician I. V. Petryanov for outstanding achievements in the field of physical and applied chemistry.<ref name="PetrMeda">Information about the Petryanov medal and the [http://fp-conference.ru/medal_petryanova/ List of its recipients] (in Russian).</ref>
